page.title: Best Waterproof Camera for Snorkeling (2026): TG-7 vs GoPro, DJI, Kodak
page.desc: The OM System Tough TG-7 wins for snorkeling photos: 50 ft waterproof with no housing, f/2.0 lens, 1 cm macro. DJI Osmo Action 5 Pro wins for video. Prices verified 2026-11-06.
page.intro:
Short answer. The best waterproof camera for snorkeling is the OM System Tough TG-7 ({buy:om-system-tough-tg-7}): waterproof to 50 ft (15 m) with no housing, an f/2.0 lens and a Microscope mode that focuses 0.4 in (1 cm) from the glass, so it takes sharper photos of fish, coral and small reef life than any action camera. You do not need a case for snorkeling: the GoPro HERO13 Black is rated to only 33 ft (10 m) on its own, and the TG-7 goes deeper than that out of the box.

If you mainly want video and wide reef scenes, the DJI Osmo Action 5 Pro wins: 66 ft (20 m) with no case, a larger 1/1.3-inch sensor and 4K at 120 fps. But it cannot focus closer than 14 in (35 cm), so small fish come out as specks. For an occasional trip on a budget, the Kodak PIXPRO WPZ2 is rated to 49 ft (15 m) at about a third of the TG-7's price, with 1080p video, a slower f/3.0 lens and a 2 in (5 cm) closest focus.

The TG-7's weak spots are a small 12 MP sensor that gets noisy in dim water, a battery rated for about 330 shots that fades fast with GPS on, and video that trails the action cameras. Owners also note a screen that is hard to read in direct sun. None of these change the pick for snorkeling stills.

page.after:
What owners complain about

Across dive forums and long-term reviews, the same TG-7 issues repeat. Battery life comes up most: the rating is about 330 shots, video drains it quickly, cold water shortens it further, and the top-mounted GPS switch is easy to flip on by accident. Reviewers and divers also say the small sensor needs light; below 20 ft or in murky water, photos get noisy without a strobe or video light. Several divers say video quality trails the GoPro and DJI, and that shooting whole reefs or schools of fish needs the optional wide-angle wet lens. Smaller gripes: the screen is not touch-sensitive and is hard to read in bright sun, the buttons and door latches are small, one store reviewer reported a sticking zoom lever, and the camera cannot shoot while charging. Flooding reports are rare and tied to door seals; check both latches and keep sand off the gaskets before every swim.

Which one by need

Photos first, especially close-ups: the TG-7. Divers on Waterpixels call it the only game in town for macro, and its f/2.0 lens and 1 cm Microscope mode are why. Video first, or one camera for surfing, biking and snorkeling: the DJI Osmo Action 5 Pro, which is rated to 66 ft on its own and has the biggest sensor here. The GoPro HERO13 Black is the same idea with a shallower 33 ft rating and a separate Macro Lens Mod for close-ups. Freediving past 50 ft: the Pentax WG-8 is rated to 66 ft but limited to two hours per session, and its f/3.5 lens is dimmer than the TG-7's. One trip a year, kids, or a tight budget: the Kodak PIXPRO WPZ2 has the same 15 m rating for far less, but only 1080p video and a 5 cm closest focus.

Not recommended

Do not buy the TG-7 as an upgrade from a TG-6; reviewers agree the changes are vertical video, USB-C and a better screen, not image quality. Do not buy any action camera for small-subject photos without its macro add-on. And do not take the TG-7 scuba diving below 50 ft without the PT-059 housing, which is rated to about 150 ft.
